Seattle plans to add up to 200 public curbside Level 2 EV charging stations by 2030, and residents can now request one near their home or apartment.
For apartment dwellers and anyone who parks on the street, that’s a useful alternative to making a separate trip to charge. More than half of Seattle’s homes are apartments or condos, according to City Light. Older houses and houseboats can also lack somewhere to plug in off the street.
Seattle City Light and the Seattle Department of Transportation are targeting neighborhoods with the fewest charging options.
The chargers are intended for topping up while parked near home. Seattle says its Level 2 curbside EV charging stations can add around 12–30 miles of range per hour, depending on the vehicle and equipment. All the new locations will be open to the public.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
City Light currently charges $0.21 per kilowatt-hour at its Level 2 chargers. At that rate, adding 30 kWh would cost $6.30. Using the utility’s estimate of about 3 miles per kWh, that’s roughly 90 miles of range, depending on the EV and driving conditions.
The expansion follows a 2023–2024 pilot at 31 locations, which SDOT says drew strong use and positive community feedback. Seattle’s installations will be funded by the transportation levy voters approved in 2024.
Residents can request a curbside charger through City Light’s program page . Applications will remain open through fall 2027, with locations reviewed and selected on an ongoing basis. The city will consider charging gaps, environmental and equity goals, and whether a site has the electrical infrastructure needed for installation.
The first installations under the expansion are scheduled to begin in fall 2027, with work continuing through 2030.

Go-Future Trike Concept Is How One British Designer Envisions Us Shopping – Built With Plastic
10 photos
Photo: Yi-Chen Jung
Some vehicles are designed to reach breakneck speeds while others are designed for more practical purposes. Today, we explore a concept that belongs to the latter category, created for nothing more than helping urban dwellers carry their groceries home. It’s called the Tesco Go-Future and while it may not be some exotic vehicle or the wildest design, it is a concept that, frankly, may just have some method to its madness.
Folks, the Go-Future is nothing more than just a concept, one from the mind of Yi-Chen Jung, a designer from Coventry, UK. While it doesn’t actually exist, at least, not in the real world , what Mr. Jung has done here may actually stand a chance of being spotted in use some day, even if that ‘day’ is in the distant future.
Photo: Yi-Chen Jung Now, the purpose of the Go-Future is exactly what I mentioned, aimed at helping shoppers make it back home with their own private three-wheeling EV. Keep in mind that the Go-Future is presented as a ‘branded’ vehicle, and in this case, owned by Tesco but it’s not; the grocery store chain offers just a setting where we can see the Go-Future at work. That’s also where this story begins.
The grocery store, whichever actually ends up choosing such a vehicle to craft a fleet that places the shopper in the center of the action, acts as a hub for the Go-Future, which also means that it’s the place where they’ll be recharged after use and stored until the next user needs one.
One detail I couldn’t work out from the ideation page that Mr. Jung displays is how these babies make it back to home base; a story for another time. It is a concept after all, so some details are sure to have been overlooked.
Photo: Yi-Chen Jung If you do need one, you’ll walk out of the store with a basket of groceries, head over to your chosen or designated Go-Future, toss the basket onto the rear hold we see in the renderings, hop inside the EV , and drive home, or be carried autonomously; it’s not quite clear how we move around just yet.
Speaking of moving, the design also includes all-weather use, or at least, light weather use, with a cabin that does lie mostly open but with the possibility to add a sort of hardtop over the occupant. But the sides of the vehicle are still missing and expose the rider to strong rains, snow, and wind.
All three of the traits above also mean that the Go-Future is not meant for the longest drives out there, but rather, as a vehicle that’s meant to travel a couple of miles at a time, a true last-mile solution. There's no mention of peak range or anything like that.
As a future mobility solution, one that’s designed to decongest our cities by taking shoppers out of busses, subways, or their own cars, Mr. Jung also paid special attention to the body of this EV, and not just by making it a single-occupancy vehicle, but the way it’s made too.
Photo: Yi-Chen Jung According to the ideation board, the Go-Future is to be crafted with a recycled body, at least, the lower half of the shell. If the design ever makes it into a real one that’s displayed at some shows like the Red Dot or iF awards, then it’s bound to get some extra points for reducing plastic waste.
This also marks the Go-Future as a concept that can see life after having carried out its duties and is decommissioned with honor. Just melt down the parts that CAN be melted down and use the goo to mold the shell of a new Go-Future. If you’ve also picked up on the fact that this makes it rather easy to replace broken parts, you’d be spot on.
Mr. Jung also mentions modularity as being part of the EV’s makeup, and from what I could make out, it’s part of the part-replacement ecosystem that Mr. Jung has worked into the design. If something breaks, it’s easy to fix. Color options also fall into the modular side of the story, with multiple available to companies to choose from.
As the saying goes, the plot thickens. The Go-Future is also designed with an app, so Mr. Jung has thought of some of the more important sides of this conceptual story, and it’s an app that is aimed at the fleet operator and the end user too.
Photo: Yi-Chen Jung All this raises one question: just how useful would something like the Go-Future be to the masses? Well, from a decongestion standpoint, this EV is smaller, so it would reduce some footprint. The second aspect that is to be considered is all that eco-friendly and recycled plastics goodness; a big win for any concept these days.
We also need to look at if it makes any sense to flood neighborhoods with these. I mean, if my grocery store is within half a mile or so to my home, I'll probably walk, except if I need some larger items, in which case, I'll call upon a car; larger items seem to be off the menu for the Go-Future too.
Maybe I'll grab a bicycle and a backpack and handle things that way. I mean, cargo e-bikes are really starting to
What I'm trying to say is that it might not make so much sense to create such a vehicle and system considering the extensive network of shops and stores in modern cities. Then again, it doesn’t hurt to dream a little.

The iX5 is set to go on sale in early 2027, but BMW is already offering a loyalty discount to sweeten the deal for those looking to stay with the brand.
BMW iX5 gets an early loyalty discount
Following the new iX3 and i3, the iX5 will go on sale in early 2027 with BMW’s Neue Klasse-inspired design, technology, and sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive system.
The iX5 is the first fully electric BMW X5. For its fifth generation, the BMW X5 will be available in gas, plug-in hybrid (PHEV), and battery electric (EV) powertrains in the US. Overseas markets will also see diesel and hydrogen fuel-cell versions.
While the gas-powered 2027 X5 40 xDrive is now available, the electric iX5 still says it’s “coming in 2027” on BMW’s website.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
BMW is already sweetening the deal with a $1,000 loyalty discount for returning buyers or lessees, according to a memo CarsDirect reviewed that was sent to dealers.
Although a $1,000 credit may not seem like much, it’s twice what BMW is offering for the 2027 iX3. The discount doesn’t require a trade-in and can be stacked with other offers.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
BMW’s loyalty discount provides a cash rebate off the MSRP when you buy or lease a new BMW through BMW Financial Services and have owned or leased another BMW within the last 12 months.
The iX5 doesn’t have any other current discounts or lease offers, but keep an eye out closer to launch.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive hits 460 kW (Source: BMW)
Earlier this week, BMW showcased the i5’s fast-charging capabilities for the first time during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic. During the event, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW said enables it to add up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.
The iX5 60 xDrive uses a massive 144 kWh battery, which BMW estimates will offer up to 435 miles of range.
Powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, the electric SUV delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque, and can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds. It can also tow up to 6,000 lbs.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive interior with M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
Inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse setup, with a wide 17.9″ central touchscreen and BMW Panoramic Vision that spans the base of the windshield. Buyers can also add the optional 14.6″ passenger screen.
Measuring 197.2″ in length, 78.7″ in width, and 68.9″ in height, the iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.
BMW will officially launch the 2027 iX5 50 xDrive in the US in the first quarter of 2027, starting at $79,800.
The iX5 is the first all-electric BMW model produced in the US. Production is set to begin at its Plant Spartanburg in South Carolina by the end of the year.

1970 Mercury Cyclone GT Sports Rare Drivetrain Layout, Marti Report Reveals Repaint
10 photos
Photo: Automotive AZ Rancher/YouTube
Introduced in 1964 as a performance-oriented version of the Comet , the Cyclone became a stand-alone model in 1968. Mercury kept it in production through 1972, with the last two iterations based on the Montego. The Cyclone was part of the muscle car wars.
Things obviously became a lot more interesting in 1966, when the Comet became an intermediate model. The larger car gained the 390-cubic-inch (6.4-liter) V8, which came with a whopping 335 horsepower on tap in S-code four-barrel carburetor form. In 1968, Mercury added the then-new 428-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Cobra Jet with 335 horsepower to the options list.
The following year, Mercury introduced the Cyclone Spoiler II, an homologation special that allowed the muscle car to join NASCAR racing. It's perhaps the most desirable Cyclone out there, but it's not the only iteration that's a rare sight today. This 1970 Cyclone GT, for instance, is also scarce.
The 1970 Cyclone was a notable upgrade over its predecessor. Mercury introduced a more aggressive front fascia, which included protruding fenders and an elongated nose. Available in base, Spoiler, and GT models, the 1970 Cyclone was available with either a 351-cubic-inch (5.8-liter) V8 or a 429-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Cobra Jet.
Like most muscle cars of the era, the Cyclone sold poorly in 1970. Records show that Mercury delivered only 13,496 units. Exactly 10,170 units were ordered in mid-range GT trim. However, the engine and transmission combo make this Cyclone GT quite the rare classic.
How so? Well, it was ordered with the N-code 429-cubic-inch V8 engine. This one's not a Cobra Jet. It was actually known as the Thunder Jet and delivered 360 horsepower (the CJ came with 370 horsepower on tap). The mill mates with a four-speed close-ratio manual, and the Marti Report says that only 192 examples were equipped with this drivetrain combo.
There's a catch, though. The powerplant is now pretty much an original block upgraded to 545-cubic-inch (8.9-liter) specs while also sporting aluminum heads. It's unclear how potent it is, but the good news is that the owner still has the original engine parts. He could revert the Cyclone to factory specs anytime.
The Mercury also got a color change. It's now wearing a Grabber Blue finish, but the Marti Report says it was actually born in Competition Orange. Well, at least both are high-impact colors, and repainting the car shouldn't be an issue. Would you restore this Cyclone back to factory specifications?
That's actually recommended if an owner wants to get most out of the car when (and if) he decides to sell. While the standard Cyclone rarely exceeds the $30,000 mark, the GT cars can fetch a lot more. Granted, the N-code 429 is not as desirable as the Cobra Jet engine, but some of these manual setups can fetch over $50,000. And I'm pretty sure I've seen at least one example go for more than $70,000 in recent years.

Humanity's First Nuclear Fission-Powered Interplanetary Spacecraft to Send Three Helicopters to Mars
9 photos
Photo: NASA
In the spring of this year, American space agency NASA held an event that would go down in history as Ignition. It was the moment when the world learned of a change in plans for the Artemis Moon exploration program, of the scrapping of the Gateway Moon space station, and of plans to launch our species' first nuclear fission-powered interplanetary spacecraft.
It is this spacecraft that brings us here now, after NASA updated the world on the progress being made. Officially called the Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the piece of tech is now in a pretty advanced stage of planning, targeting launch as soon as 2028.
SR-1 is both the name of the reactor and the spacecraft that will be used to deliver to the surface of the Red Planet a trio of exploration helicopters collectively called SkyFall. Its main and key element, the nuclear power module, is what now comes under the spotlight.
Installed at the back of the spacecraft's boom, the nuclear reactor, whose exact components and features are still kept under wraps, will be used to generate heat through nuclear fission. A conversion system is then used to convert the resulting heat into electricity, which will be to power the ship's power systems and electric propulsion.
The conversion system in question is of the Brayton cycle variety, a thermodynamic arrangement that uses a gas as a working fluid to convert thermal energy into electrical power. This part of the ship is now being put together by a company called Sierra Lobo.
Photo: AeroVironment This element will be integrated with the fission reactor itself, presently in the works over at the Department of Energy (DOE)’s Idaho National Laboratory. NASA says it is now working with the DOE to make the reactor as safe to operate as possible.
As humanity’s first fission-powered spacecraft to travel outside Earth’s orbit, Freedom will head for Mars, but its projected success is likely to change designs for future spacecraft heading elsewhere in the solar system as well.
Closer to our time, that would be the development of something called the Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1), a surface power system that will be attached to the upcoming Moon Base to keep it going when the Moon goes through its long periods of darkness and cold.
That setup will be a tad more complex, and that's why NASA decided it would fly the reactor first, without having to devise a lander that would be required to place the hardware on the surface of the Moon.
Photo: AeroVironment As said, the nuclear fission reactor that's now in the process of being built will deliver to Mars three exploration helicopters. Inspired by the tiny Ingenuity, a tiny helicopter-like drone that proved, for the first time, that powered, controlled flight on another planet is possible.
The helos are being developed by NASA with help from American company AeroVironment , which was also involved in the Ingenuity project, and they will be deployed on the Red Planet mid-air from inside an entry capsule.
Without having to rely on a lander to get them to the surface, each of the three helos will be equipped with quite a lot of instruments, including ground-penetrating radar, imagers, and cameras to snap photos of the surface of the planet below.
These tools will be deployed to measure air temperature, wind speed and direction, and data about subsurface features. The bits of info will then be used to map the terrain and characterize features of Mars that have never been studied before, including at different elevations.
Photo: AeroVironment The goal of the SkyFall mission is to identify potential water sources, subsurface ice, and generate a meteorological data set.
NASA is presently in the process of identifying a suitable landing place for the helicopters, which, despite being deployed directly into the atmosphere, will have to land now and then. The agency says it is looking for flat, low-elevation areas that are free of geological obstacles, from where the three machines could technically operate for years on end.
The three machines are in a pretty advanced stage of development as well. The last time we heard anything about them was back in the summer of this year, when we were told a thing or two about the testing currently taking place.
As for the piece of tech that inspired the SkyFall mission, and, indirectly, Space Reactor-1 Freedom, the little Ingenuity drone that could flew for a total of 10.5 miles (17.0 km) over the course of 72 flights, covering a distance of 10.5 miles (17.0 km) and spending a combined two hours in the thin Martian air.
We are not told, at least for now, anything about the capabilities of the nuclear tech that forms the backbone of the Space Reactor-1 Freedom spacecraft. That means, among other things, that we don't know how fast it will go, and how much time it will spend en route to the Red Planet, a distance that's presently covered in about nine months.

FreightWaves’ F3: Future of Freight Festival returns to Chattanooga next week, with sessions on AI adoption, autonomous trucking and the technologies reshaping freight operations taking center stage.
The event, held Oct. 27-28 at The Signal at Chattanooga Choo Choo, will feature keynote presentations, fireside chats, technology demonstrations and discussions about how companies are applying new tools to transportation and logistics.
Registration and ticket options are available through the official F3 website . Published group rates range from $895 to $1,095 per person, depending on group size, while bundled tickets cost $1,895 for F3 and the Brokerage Compliance Symposium or $1,995 for F3 and the Awards Dinner, which is scheduled for Oct. 26.
The Freight Brokerage Compliance Symposium will take place the day before F3, on Oct. 26, from 8:45 a.m. to 4 p.m. at The Signal. The separate event will cover carrier liability, fraud, Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration rules, cargo theft, insurance and other compliance risks. Registration costs $495, plus taxes and fees, and is required separately from F3 unless attendees purchase a bundle.
For freight technology companies and their customers, a central question is how emerging tools translate into practical improvements in day-to-day operations.
AI adoption moves beyond the hype
Artificial intelligence features prominently in this year’s agenda, with sessions examining both its potential and the challenges of putting it to work.
A discussion titled “Beyond the Hype: What AI in Freight Actually Delivers When the Noise Dies Down” is scheduled for 2 p.m. Oct. 28. Prasad Gollapalli, founder and CEO of Qued, will join FreightWaves founder and CEO Craig Fuller to examine the practical value of AI in the industry.
At 2:20 p.m. on the same day, Nilkanth Patel of Pallet and FreightWaves’ Julie Van de Kamp will discuss lessons from AI deployment, including decisions about whether to build technology internally or buy it from outside providers.
Another discussion, “Beyond AI: How Autonomous Execution Is Redefining Freight Operations,” is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. Oct. 27. Robert Nathan of Envoy AI and Van de Kamp will explore how AI and autonomous software can execute freight workflows rather than simply provide information or recommendations.
Autonomous trucking and freight data
Autonomous trucking will also feature heavily in the program. A roundtable titled “The State of Autonomous Trucking: From Yards to Highways” is scheduled for 2:45 p.m. on Oct. 27. Brett Suma of Bot Auto , Earl Adams of PlusAI and Mike McGahn of Forterra will join FreightWaves’ Thomas Wasson to talk about the technology’s development and potential applications.
The agenda also includes a Tesla Semi ride-along opportunity from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Oct. 27 and from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Oct. 28 at The Signal, offering attendees a closer look at the electric truck.
Freight data is another major theme. SONAR, FreightWaves’ freight market data and analytics platform, will host a session titled “Beyond the Dashboard: The AI-Powered Future of Freight Data” from 4 to 4:45 p.m. Oct. 27 in the Barber Boardroom at the Hotel Chalet. The session will be led by a member of SONAR’s team.
Other SONAR sessions include “ Bid Season Blastoff: Turn Market Intelligence into Better Bids” on Oct. 28, followed by “Put the Data to Work: SONAR Use Cases You Can Steal,” which will focus on applying freight data to business decisions.
Rapid-fire technology demonstrations are also scheduled throughout both days, giving companies an opportunity to show attendees how their products work.
Awards to be announced
The F3 Awards Dinner will open the week on Oct. 26, from 5 to 9 p.m. at The Signal. FreightWaves will recognize its 2027 FreightTech 100 honorees and announce the FreightTech25 , while also announcing the Shipper of Choice winners.
The 2027 FreightTech 100, announced in September, includes 100 companies selected for innovation across freight and supply chain technology. More than half of this year’s honorees did not appear in the 2026 FreightTech 100, reflecting constant innovation in a market that includes transportation management systems, shipment visibility, fleet technology, AI and automation.
An independent panel of more than 80 industry executives ranks the 2027 FreightTech 100 companies to determine the FreightTech25.
The awards dinner will also feature the announcement of the FreightTech Vanguard Award winner, which recognizes logistics pioneers, founders and companies whose technologies have had a lasting impact on transportation and the supply chain.
The awards provide one view of which companies are gaining recognition across the industry. The festival’s sessions and demonstrations offer another: a chance to hear how operators and technology providers are approaching the challenges of implementing new tools.
Together, the events will give attendees an opportunity to assess where freight technology is making progress, where practical questions remain and which developments could shape transportation and logistics in the coming year.
Why this matters
Freight technology companies face growing pressure to prove their tools can deliver measurable results, from improving efficiency to reducing costs. F3 will bring technology providers and freight operators together to discuss how AI, autonomous trucking and data analytics are being applied across the industry, offering a look at which innovations are moving toward real-world adoption.

source_document.body:
Autonomous robots are intelligent machines that can perceive their environment, make decisions based on real-time conditions, and perform tasks without constant human direction.
Key Takeaways
Autonomous robots can perceive their environment, make decisions, and act without constant human guidance.
Unlike traditional automation, autonomous robots can adapt when conditions change rather than simply following predefined instructions.
Modern warehouse autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) help maintain operational flow by responding to real-time conditions and shifting priorities.
Autonomous robots are increasingly used across logistics, eCommerce, warehousing, manufacturing, healthcare, biotech, data centers, and research environments.
The most effective autonomous systems coordinate robots, software, and people to improve flexibility, productivity, and operational performance.
What Do Autonomous Robots Do?
Autonomous robots can perceive their environment, make decisions, and execute tasks without constant human direction. Unlike traditional automated systems that follow predefined instructions, autonomous robots can respond to changing conditions in real time.
In warehouse environments, autonomy goes beyond independent movement. It also includes how robots adapt to changing conditions, prioritize work, and operate as part of a broader system that keeps fulfillment moving efficiently.
What are the Core Components of an Autonomous Robot?
Autonomous robots rely on three core capabilities: perception, decision-making, and actuation.
Perception: Sensors such as LiDAR and cameras help robots understand their environment and detect changing conditions.
Decision-making: Software evaluates real-time information and determines the most appropriate action.
Actuation: Motors and mechanical systems translate decisions into physical movement or task execution.
Together, these capabilities allow autonomous robots to operate safely and adapt to changing environments without constant human direction. In more advanced systems, they also extend to prioritizing tasks, adjusting workflows, and coordinating with other systems on the warehouse floor.
How do Autonomous Robots Work Within Larger Systems?
Autonomous robots are rarely deployed in isolation. In modern warehouse operations, they are part of a broader system designed to coordinate movement, tasks, and workflows across the entire facility.
An autonomous system brings together robots, software, and people to keep work moving in a structured and adaptable way. Instead of focusing on a single task, like moving inventory from one point to another, these systems manage how work flows from receiving through picking, packing, and shipping.
This matters because warehouse operations don’t run in silos. What happens in picking affects packing. When packing slows down, outbound flow starts to back up. And when inbound isn’t aligned with demand, replenishment can’t keep up. Each part of the operation is connected.
Autonomous systems are designed to account for that connection. They help coordinate tasks across workflows, adjust priorities in real time, and maintain balance across the floor as conditions change.
In practice, that can look like:
Redirecting robots to support picking when order volume spikes
Adjusting task priority to prevent pack stations from getting buried
Routing inventory dynamically based on current demand
Maintaining steady flow even when labor availability shifts mid-shift
As these systems evolve, the focus has moved beyond individual robot capabilities to how effectively the entire operation can respond to change. The goal isn’t just to automate tasks - it’s to keep work flowing consistently, even when demand, labor, and order profiles don’t line up as expected.
This shift is what defines modern autonomy in the warehouse. It’s not just about what a robot can do on its own, but how the system works together to maintain performance across the operation.
What Is the Difference Between Automation and Autonomy?
The difference between automation and autonomy is adaptability. Automated systems follow predefined instructions, while autonomous robots can interpret conditions and adjust their actions in real time.
A common misunderstanding is that any machine performing a task automatically is “autonomous.” In reality, many automated systems rely on predefined routes, manual programming, or direct human control. They can execute tasks consistently, but they cannot adapt when conditions change.
The distinction between automation and autonomy lies in adaptability. Automated systems follow instructions. Autonomous robots can interpret their environment, make decisions in real time, and adjust their actions as conditions evolve.
For example, equipment on a traditional car assembly line is often described as robotics. These systems are highly effective within controlled environments because they execute the same programmed movement repeatedly. However, if something unexpected occurs, they typically cannot recognize the issue or alter their behavior.
Consider a machine responsible for placing a spare tire into a car trunk. If the trunk were closed unexpectedly, the machine would continue executing its programmed motion because it lacks the ability to understand that conditions have changed.
A truly autonomous robot would behave differently. It would detect that the environment had changed, stop the task, evaluate the situation, and determine an appropriate next action.
The same principle applies in warehouse operations. When autonomous mobile robots encounter aisle congestion, changing order priorities, or unexpected obstacles, they can reroute, reprioritize work, and continue operating without requiring manual intervention. As warehouse operations become more dynamic, that ability to respond in real time, and not simply follow instructions, is what defines autonomy in practice.
What is an Example of an Autonomous Robot ?
The Roomba is one of the most widely recognized autonomous robots. It operates independently within a dynamic environment, making decisions based on what it perceives in real time.
Using onboard sensors, it maps its surroundings, avoids obstacles, and adjusts its path as conditions change. It doesn’t follow a fixed route or require manual direction to complete its task.
That same principle applies in warehouse environments.
When an autonomous robot encounters an obstacle, such as a pallet, congestion in an aisle, or a change in task priority, it can adjust in the moment. It reroutes, continues working, and maintains flow without requiring intervention.
At a basic level, an autonomous robot determines what action to take based on what it observes. In a warehouse, that ability directly impacts how consistently work moves through the operation.
Simply put, an autonomous robot is one that decides the action it should take on its own based on information it has perceived to increase productivity. If you would like to learn more about autonomous robots or their endless possible applications, contact us today . If you’re unsure how robotics technology could help you, here are 8 great autonomous robot examples.
1. Autonomous Robots for Logistics
One of the most common applications of autonomous robots is material transport . Moving inventory across a warehouse or fulfillment center is labor-intensive and often involves significant walking time.
By handling these repetitive movements, robots help reduce travel time and allow associates to stay focused on productive tasks like picking and packing.
2. Mobile Autonomous Robots for eCommerce
eCommerce operations place unique demands on warehouses, with high order volumes, fast turnaround times, and constant variability in order profiles.
Autonomous robots support eCommerce workflows such as:
Order fulfillment
Returns handling
Sortation and consolidation
Inventory movement and staging
Their flexibility allows operations to adjust quickly as demand shifts throughout the day.
3. Autonomous Robots for Warehousing
Modern warehouses are large, complex environments where maintaining flow is critical. Autonomous robots support core workflows such as:
Moving inventory between zones
Replenishment and restocking
Assisting with picking and consolidation
A key capability is their ability to navigate open, dynamic spaces. Using sensors and mapping technology, they can operate safely alongside people while adjusting to changing conditions on the floor.
As these systems evolve, they are increasingly used across multiple workflows - not just a single task - helping coordinate activity across the operation.
4. Autonomous Robots and Mobile Manipulators for Manufacturing
Manufacturing environments benefit from flexibility as production needs shift.
Beyond transporting in-process parts and finished goods, autonomous robots integrated with accessories such as conveyors or robotic arms, can assist in the production process. For example, AMRs with robotic arms can sort, pick, and pack products with the added ability to dynamically move to multiple locations.
Static conveyors have long been used in line work, as they help speed up production and sorting. Adding a conveyor onto an autonomous robot means that conveyor capabilities can now be flexible and mobile. Autonomous robots with built-in conveyors can connect to static conveyors to move products more effectively throughout a facility.
Autonomous robots with attachments that can lift loads and connect to carts allow the robots to load and unload payloads and, in some cases, connect to carts without human intervention. This combination of the cart transport and loading/unloading in one autonomous robot is a relatively new capability, but one that will create more potential applications for autonomous robots.
5. Autonomous Robots for Data Centers
In data centers and secure facilities, autonomous robots are used to transport sensitive materials while maintaining strict chain-of-custody requirements.
They provide consistent, trackable movement of high-value assets while reducing manual handling.
6. Autonomous Robots in Healthcare
Healthcare facilities use autonomous robots to transport supplies, medications, and equipment throughout hospitals.
They are also used for sanitation , with systems equipped to disinfect spaces without exposing staff to unnecessary risk. These applications help improve efficiency while supporting safety protocols.
7. Autonomous Robots in Biotech
Biotech environments often require continuous monitoring and strict process control.
Autonomous robots assist with routine tasks such as sampling, material handling, and waste management. By taking on these repetitive workflows, they allow skilled workers to focus on analysis and decision-making.
8. Autonomous Robots for Research and Development
In research environments, autonomous robots are used to handle repetitive transport tasks and support experimentation.
They also serve as platforms for developing new technologies, such as advanced sensors and robotic manipulation systems, allowing teams to test and iterate more efficiently.
Ready to Explore Autonomous Warehouse Operations?
Autonomous robots are no longer limited to moving inventory from point A to point B. Modern autonomous robots can help warehouses improve operational flow, reduce unproductive travel, and adapt more effectively as business conditions change.

COLOGNE, Germany — The Danish government plans to buy two types of “long-range,” precision-strike missiles, one air-launched and one ground-launched, to retaliate against adversaries after an attack on the country, officials announced on Thursday.
The shopping list includes the Kongsberg-made Joint Strike Missile, which F-35 fighter aircraft can carry, and the Anthem missile by U.S.-based company Covenant as a ground-launched option, Defense Minister Jeppe Bruus said.
Officials released few details, leaving open the question of when the armed forces would receive the missiles, how many of them and at what cost, broadcaster TV2 reported in a live blog of a defense ministry press conference about the planned acquisitions.
Long-range missiles are very much en vogue in Europe at the moment, as countries are equipping themselves as a deterrent against Russian aggression. Governments here consider the capability to strike back on their own all the more urgent because U.S. assistance with such weaponry in case of a conflict is considered uncertain under the presidency of Donald Trump.
The ranges of strike missiles labeled as long-range are a bit of a guessing game, as manufacturers and governments keep performance information close to their chests so as to avoid tipping off adversaries. Typically, they fall in the range of 500 kilometers to 1,500 kilometers, depending on engine and warhead configurations.
Danish officials cite a NATO contribution target as a key motivator for the envisioned weapons class, which would constitute a qualitatively new capability for the small country, according to TV2. Copenhagen is on the hook to offer the alliance a long-range strike capability by 2030, according to the defense ministry.
“These acquisitions represent a significant step toward improving Denmark’s self-defense capabilities, strengthening NATO, and enhancing our capacity to strike back,” Defense Minister Bruus was quoted as saying in an agency statement.
According to TV2, the envisioned Anthem missiles for Denmark, which have never seen combat, are to be produced in Germany. Manufacturer Covenant announced a new production site in Leipzig, Germany, last month, claiming it could churn out missiles there beginning in early 2027.
The German defense ministry has so far said only that there are talks with Covenant about buying the weapons to plug Germany’s long-range strike gap.
The manufacturer’s pitch is that Anthem missiles will be cheaper than products available on the market now. Reuters has previously reported a mid-six-figure target price per unit set by company executives during serial production.

Union Pacific reported record third-quarter revenue and profits as higher volume , pricing, and efficiency gains more than offset the impact of rising fuel prices and inflation.
“Union Pacific’s third-quarter results demonstrate our ability to safely deliver the service we sold our customers while efficiently handling 6% volume growth,” Chief Executive Jim Vena said on the railroad’s (NYSE: UNP ) earnings call today.
Operating income increased 15%, to $2.94 billion, as revenue grew 15%, to $7.19 billion. Earnings per share rose 16%, to $3.49.
The railroad’s operating ratio was 59.1%, a 0.1-point improvement compared to a year ago. Workforce productivity, measured by car-miles per employee, improved 5%.
Overall volume was up 6% for the quarter. Premium volume — which includes intermodal and automotive traffic — was up 9%. Industrial products traffic grew 6% in the quarter, while bulk volume was flat.
“Domestic intermodal delivered its fifth consecutive record quarter in both volume and revenue. Our foundation of service combined with strong business development and the deployment of buffer resources enabled 13% volume growth,” said Kenny Rocker, executive vice president of marketing and sales. “International intermodal volumes improved 8% versus last year driven by strong West Coast import volumes and business wins.”
The carrier offered a positive outlook for fourth-quarter volume, as high fuel prices and tight truck capacity will continue to drive conversions of truckload freight to rail. The lone exception is coal volume, which will remain under pressure due to low natural gas prices and high utility stockpiles.
Rocker expects a third straight year of record domestic intermodal volume.
Overall volume growth prompted UP to shift some capital spending planned for next year into this year. UP now expects to spend $3.5 billion on capital projects this year, up from $3.3 billion.
UP’s key operational metrics improved slightly compared to last year, with car miles per day up 1%, average train speed flat, and terminal dwell down by 2%. Train length grew 2%, to an average of 9,969 feet.
“Operating discipline and consistent execution of the fundamentals drove another quarter of record workforce productivity, record train length, and record fuel consumption,” said Eric Gehringer, executive vice president of operations.
The railroad said its employee personal injury and train accident rates improved compared to the three-year rolling average but did not provide specifics.

Tesla says it’s building its own maps to fix some of the most common problems with its “Full Self-Driving” system, including reading speed limits, parking, and choosing routes. The company’s head of AI described the effort on Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call.
It’s a notable shift for a company whose CEO spent years arguing that self-driving systems relying on maps are brittle. And it shows Tesla’s fleet is now doing the same job Waymo’s cars do: mapping the roads so the self-driving system knows what it can’t reliably figure out on its own.
Tesla fans argue that Waymo’s approach differs because it creates HD maps with lidar, but ultimately both are creating their own maps; if your argument is that Tesla’s maps are less well-defined and needed for driving for different reasons than Waymo’s, you don’t really have an argument.
What Tesla said about maps
The question came from Tesla’s shareholder Q&A. A retail investor wrote that mapping “continues to be a problem” for FSD, listing speed limits, parking and typical routes as the three biggest issues, and asked why Tesla relies on third-party maps instead of its own.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Tesla’s VP of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, agreed that “we shouldn’t be depending on external people’s maps.” He said Tesla is building its own maps using a new AI-based mapping and navigation architecture, fed by what the fleet collectively learns, that will also learn individual drivers’ preferences and respond to voice commands.
He said the technology will start handling the beginning and end of trips with FSD v15, and over the following months take over navigation, parking and destination handling.
Tesla’s history with maps
Tesla has gone back and forth on this before.
In 2015, when it launched Autopilot, Tesla told Fortune it had started building high-precision maps with “100 times the level of granularity” of standard navigation, using data from its customer cars.
At its Autonomy Day in 2019, Elon Musk said Tesla had tried high-precision lane maps and realized it was “a huge mistake.” He called relying on them a “really bad idea” that makes a self-driving system “extremely brittle,” in the same presentation where he called lidar a “fool’s errand.” The message was clear: Waymo needed lidar and detailed maps, and Tesla would solve driving with cameras and AI alone, anywhere.
Seven years later, Tesla is building a map layer from its own fleet to fix the things its vision system gets wrong.
It comes down to understanding the environment
To be fair to Tesla, this isn’t an HD map in the sense Musk criticized. Tesla has always used navigation maps, and building its own instead of licensing them isn’t a contradiction on its own.
But look at the problems Tesla is trying to fix. Speed limits, parking and routes are all about understanding the environment, and FSD still often fails at it, especially with speed limit signs.
Last month, a Belgian road safety group found that FSD sped in 55% of the 30 km/h zones it tested in Brussels , averaging 44 km/h, partly because the car’s screen showed a 50 km/h limit in most of those zones. In the US, NHTSA is weighing an investigation into claims that Tesla Robotaxis speed through active school zones , covering about 1,000 Model Y and Cybercab vehicles.
A speed limit sign is about as simple as road information gets. If an end-to-end vision system can’t reliably read and apply it, and the fix is a better map, then vision alone isn’t doing the job Tesla said it would.
Tesla’s fleet is now a mapping fleet
That brings Tesla closer to Waymo than it would like to admit.
Waymo maps a city by driving its sensor-equipped vehicles through it before launching service, and keeps those maps updated as its fleet drives. Tesla is now describing the same idea: its cars collect what they see, and that data feeds a Tesla-built map that helps every car drive better. The main difference is that Waymo’s cars have lidar on top.
It also fits how Tesla’s Robotaxi service actually operates: city by city, inside small geofenced service areas , with Tesla handling the fleet operations. Tesla isn’t talking about centimeter-level HD maps today, but a fleet-built map that keeps getting more detailed could easily head that way.
Electrek’s Take
There’s nothing wrong with using maps. Every serious self-driving program does, and a map built from millions of Tesla cars could be a real advantage. If it fixes FSD’s speed limit problems, that’s good news for everyone sharing the road with it.
What’s wrong is the years of messaging that Tesla’s approach didn’t need any of this. Musk sold FSD as a general solution that would work anywhere through vision alone, while dismissing Waymo’s maps and lidar as crutches. Now Tesla is adding the map, it already operates in geofences, and the AI still can’t reliably read a 30 km/h sign in Brussels.
Waymo built its maps and has been running a driverless service for years. Tesla is building its maps now and has pushed unsupervised FSD in customer cars to Q2 2027 , and only inside its Robotaxi fleet. At what point do we admit that both companies are solving the same problem in very similar ways, and only one of them has lidar?
We are a decade into Tesla’s self-driving effort and it is doing exactly what Musk used to say doesn’t count as a “true self-driving system”: geo-fenced areas using maps.

22-Year-Old Grandson Drives His Grandma's 1981 Lincoln Continental, It's a Luxury Lounge on Wheels
33 photos
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube
He is 22 years old and drives a car that is 45 years old. This 1981 Lincoln Continental Mark VI has been in the family since new and is there to stay. Even though everybody takes it out for a spin every once in a while, he has become its custodian and has to make sure everything works like it did when the Lincoln rolled off the production line.
The 1981 Lincoln Continental Mark VI is actually his grandma's car. It was a birthday gift for her when she turned 40. She got it from her husband and two children. They searched for the safest car for a lady at the time. So they chose the Continental because of the long hood, which provided a big crumple zone in case she crashed.
They bought it brand-new from the dealership, drove it home, and parked it in the driveway to surprise the birthday girl. It has been with the family ever since and it is not going anywhere. The 45-year-old Lincoln still has the dealer tag on the decklid.
Everything is original on the car, except for the tires and the Motorcraft 7200 Variable Venturi carburetor, which broke right after the warranty expired. While the Canadian-spec cars were built with a carburetor, Ford equipped all U.S. market 1981 Mark VIs with the first-generation Central Fuel Injection (CFI) system.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube Raphael is in charge of making sure it is well maintained and that everything works. He loves his cars reliable and fully functional. No surprise there for the young man who is fully dedicated to preserving a 45-year-old piece of family history.
The car is inching closer to the 100,000-mile moment. No major issues over all these years. He has recently checked the steering and the suspension, and they work properly. However, the air conditioning system is leaking and needs constant recharging.
The paint, with very few flaws, looks like it did the day it was first driven home. The car has never seen winter, snow, or salt. It spends the cold, snowy period locked inside the family's garage, driving out only when the summer comes, when the weather is warm, and the streets are clean.
This time, Raphael is making a 373-mile (600-kilometer) round trip from British Columbia to brag about his Lincoln to TJ Lamb of Magnacars . It took him five hours to reach his destination. He drove at around 56 mph (90 kph) and says it has been his most comfortable road trip ever. " It's a rolling couch with a V8 ."
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube Raphael's car is the Signature Series, which was the absolute peak of the Mark VI lineup, sitting above the standard models and even the Designer Editions. Back in 1981, the Signature Series was limited to just two color schemes: Red and Silver.
Unlike the standard Mark VIs, which often came with contrasting vinyl roofs and pinstriping, his car features the solid burgundy red body paint paired with a matching Burgundy Valino vinyl landau roof, heavily textured to resemble premium leather grain, in a highly exclusive color-coordinated scheme, which was the exclusive package for the Signature Series.
The car features the vacuum-operated hidden headlamps, an upright grille, the distinct gold-toned Signature Series emblems next to the opera windows, and the spare-tire hump molded into the trunk lid, which doesn't actually host the spare tire.
The Continental Mark VI was way ahead of its era. It came with a digital instrument panel, a multi-function trip computer, which can switch from miles to kilometers and back to miles in the blink of an eye, automatic climate control, and an integrated garage door opener, because the Signature Series featured nearly every available option.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube All in a maxed-out cabin that looks like a luxury lounge. The seats sport a distinct, ultra-plush pillow-top design with separate, button-tufted cushions. They were available in either Dark Cordovan premium leather or a luxurious velour, like this car features.
Furthermore, the interior features thicker door-pull straps, unique woodgrain appliques, and a matching plushly carpeted lower door portion. When bought new, these cars came with a leather-bound owner's manual case and a special Signature Series tool kit or flashlight stored in the glovebox.
The Lincoln is also equipped with an outside temperature gauge, built directly into the driver’s side exterior rearview mirror. The gauge uses an old-school, bimetallic spring coil that contracts and expands based on the ambient air temperature.
The Mark VI transitioned to Ford's body-on-frame Panther platform. This engineering shift made the car 14 inches shorter and over 1,100 pounds lighter than the Mark V it replaced. However, at 219.1 inches (5,565 millimeters) and sitting on a wheelbase of 117.1 inches (2,974 millimeters), it was still a landyacht.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube The small-block V8 from under the hood has to pull a car that tips the scales at 4,142 pounds (1,879 kilograms). The 302-cubic-inch (5.0-liter) Windsor engine pushes out 130 horsepower (132 metric horsepower) and 230 pound-feet (312 Newton meters) of torque.
It takes forever to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 14.0 long seconds on its way to a top speed of 101 mph (163 kph), while the gas-thirsty small-block drinks up 13.84 MPG (17 l/100 km). A four-speed AOD automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels. This is what Raphael will drive home.

ISA Yachts' Newest Superyacht Design Has Three Panoramic Lounges, Two Garages, and a Wellness Center
15 photos
Photo: ISA Yachts
Each new yacht design developed by ISA Yachts, a division of the Palumbo Superyachts group, is a work of art, impressing with sleek looks and ultra-modern resort amenities. The recently unveiled Poseidon is no exception.
Poseidon is a 282-foot (86-meter) superyacht concept that perfectly embodies futuristic maritime luxury. It is the product of a longtime collaboration between the technical department of Palumbo Superyachts and talented Venetian designer Enrico Gobbi of Team for Design, and it was introduced as part of ISA's Large Yacht Collection.
Headquartered in Ancona, Italy, ISA Yachts was founded in 2001 specifically for the construction of high-end custom yachts, superyachts, and large projects, and over the years, it has become a market leader that prides itself on efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery.
The newly revealed Poseidon is the fourth design presented as part of the ISA Large Yacht Collection, a platform for large custom yachts developed around a shared engineering framework. Initially introduced in July, the ISA Large Yacht Collection also includes the 269-foot (82-meter) Amarcord 82 and 282-foot (86-meter) Amarcord 86, both developed by Nuvolari Lenard, and the 269-foot (82-meter) Essence by Lobanov Studio.
Photo: ISA Yachts At 282 feet long with a 12.8-meter (42-foot) beam, Poseidon distinguishes itself as one of the largest projects based on the platform. It’s an innovative vessel that breaks traditional design boundaries by separating dedicated entertainment spaces from absolute private luxury, and according to the yard, it’s designed to deliver a perfect “balance of elegance, dynamism, and generous interior volumes.”
The yacht’s sleek exterior profile is a blend of modern and classic lines. A high, gently curved bow gives it a classic outline, while the long forward section and the superstructure positioned toward the stern lend it a more contemporary vibe. Thanks to this configuration, the vessel has both a cascade of open water-facing terraces and a tiered stern architecture with outdoor decks sloping downward toward the water.
Moreover, inspired by the dynamism of sports cars, the designer created a slimmer profile and added lateral air intakes, sculpted surfaces, and softer geometries that create an interplay of volumes and movement. Long sweeping lines from bow to stern contribute to the yacht’s elegance and gracious presence on the water, while extensive glazing completes the modern look.
Photo: ISA Yachts Special attention has been paid to creating a strong relationship between the yacht and the sea. To that end, Poseidon features low-profile bulwarks that help keep open sightlines, as well as a series of terraces that extend across multiple levels.
One of the outstanding features of the concept is its stern area, which includes a spacious beach club designed for relaxation and wellness. It comes with fold-down platforms on both sides to extend the water-side area, connecting the interior lounge to the surrounding sea. The beach club also incorporates a bar and a glass-sided whirlpool tub.
Wellness amenities have become must-have onboard features on modern luxury yachts , so it’s no surprise that Poseidon also has a dedicated wellness area amidships. Accessed via a passageway from the beach club area, it includes a gym, sauna, steam room, treatment rooms, and massage facilities, along with two additional opening balconies that let guests do yoga or other activities in the open air.
Photo: ISA Yachts The main deck’s outdoor area is a great space for relaxation and sunbathing. It’s organized around a large T-shaped swimming pool that incorporates a whirlpool section. This pool is integrated into the stern design, with a glazed structure surrounding it and an architectural detail resembling a sports car spoiler framing its upper edge. Integrated lighting highlight the glass surfaces and the structure’s geometric lines in the dark.
No renderings of the interior living quarters have been revealed yet, but the interior salon on the main deck is said to be configured with a “conversation area,” which probably means a generous seating arrangement. It also includes a cinema and a formal dining area.
In terms of sleeping arrangements, the layout can be configured either with six staterooms for up to 12 guests or seven cabins for a maximum of 14. The layout also takes into account the separation of guest and crew circulation.
As on any luxury superyacht , the owner of Poseidon will benefit from a generous private area. In fact, the entire upper deck is dedicated to the owner, and it includes a private suite with 360-degree glazing, a study, a dressing room and a bathroom with a double shower and bathtub. This private haven also benefits from direct access to the forward outdoor area, which is fitted with a second T-shaped pool surrounded by sunbathing spaces. This front deck can also be used as a touch-and-go helipad.
The aft section of the upper deck includes a comfortable indoor lounge which seamlessly connects to an al-fresco dining area offering seating for up to 14 people.
Photo: ISA Yachts Another space dedicated to relaxation can be found on the bridge deck. Here, an additional panoramic sky lounge allows guests to unwind while enjoying beautiful vistas of the ocean. Its roofline draws inspiration from a sports car cockpit, and the space also includes a Jacuzzi.
For tenders and toys, Poseidon has not one but two garages, one located forward and one amidships. Set to be constructed with a steel hull and aluminum superstructure, the yacht boasts a full-load draught of 11.8 feet (3.6 meters). It will be powered by two MTU 16V4000M63L engines, each producing 2,240 kW, and ISA Yachts estimates a maximum speed of 17 knots, a cruising speed of 14 knots, and a range of approximately 5,000 nautical miles at 12 knots.
According to Palumbo Superyachts’ Director Giuseppe Palumbo, the new Poseidon superyacht concept represents a prime example of the shipyard’s direction. “The 86-meter Poseidon [is] a project with a strong personality, developed on a solid engineering foundation, confirming our ability to offer increasingly sophisticated and distinctive custom solutions,” he explained.

Largest Boeing 737 MAX Cleared to Fly With Updates to the Systems That Caused Two Crashes
11 photos
Photo: Boeing
They call it the 737-10, and it is the newest and largest version of the Boeing 737 MAX family. How large would that be? Think 230 passengers in maximum seating configuration, something that, for a single-aisle airplane, is quite something.
As you know, the 737 MAX has a pretty troubled history, with two crashes that occurred back in 2018 and 2019 leading to the entire fleet that existed at that time being grounded all over the world between March 2019 and December 2020.
That hasn't stopped Boeing in its tracks, though, and the company has been hard at work making the planes as safe as they can be. This new version is the first to incorporate some of these changes right off the factory floor.
The 737-10 is the latest addition to the family, joining the existing 737-7, 737-8, 737-8-200, and 737-9. What makes it different, aside from the revised safety systems we'll discuss later on, is that fact that it carry the largest number of passenger.
Photo: Boeing Technically speaking, operators can spec the plane to be able to move between 185 and 230 passengers, seated in two classes. The maximum range the aircraft can reach is 3,566 miles (5,740 km), making it ideal for use on some of the most popular routes. Also, that's 420 miles (676 km) more than what competitor planes without auxiliary fuel tanks offer.
Earlier this week, Boeing said the plane finally got its Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certification (after several years of delays), something that clears it to fly in American skies and thus opens the doors for Boeing to start making deliveries and please both airlines and customers – supposedly, the plane will offer the lowest per-seat costs of any single-aisle airplane currently in operation.
To get here, says the company, a total of around 1,000 flight tests have been performed, totaling more than 2,000 flight hours, but also 1,000 hours of ground tests. At the end of it all, the 737-10 became the first commercial airplane to be certified to the provisions of the harsher 2020 Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act (ACSAA).
Perhaps the most important thing about the plane is that it incorporates a solution that should address the issue that led to the crash of Lion Air Flight 610 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, which took 346 lives. That would be, above all, an enhanced Angle-of-Attack system (AoA).
Photo: Boeing The crashes mentioned above were caused by one of the two AoA sensors fitted on the outside of the planes feeding wrong data to the plane's Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS). As a result, the tech continuously pitched the nose of the planes down, regardless of the efforts made by the pilots to correct it.
Boeing now says that the AoAs on the 737-10 benefit from no less than five monitoring systems that track the way the sensors operate at takeoff, after takeoff, and in case they go through a bird strike. If an error is detected, the system steps in and prevents it from propagating to other systems that might impact the safety of the flight.
The error will be communicated to the pilots through an AoA Fail alert shown on the primary displays, accompanied by details about which of the two sensors is responsible for the error. This, says Boeing, also eliminates the pilots' need to go through an extensive checklist so that they could identify the problem.
As a sort of redundancy system, the cockpit now comes with a physical switch pilots can use to turn off the stick shaker, the tech that lets pilots know their aircraft is approaching a stall condition.
Photo: Boeing In the two crashes caused by the AoA and MCAS, the sensor error propagated to the stick shaker as well, making pilots believe they're rapidly approaching the moment their plane will fall from the sky – something that complicated matters even more for the ones involved.
Despite the troubles the 737 Max went through, the industry doesn't seem too scared. When it comes to the 737-10 alone, for instance, there are some 1,555 planes waiting to be delivered, which amount to around 30 percent of the order book for the entire family, which stands at 7,350 orders.
Boeing says the revised sensors and the other modifications made to the 737-10 will be retrofitted on other models of the family already in service, but does not mention how many planes that is, or when the retrofitting will begin. All other versions to be produced from now on will incorporate the upgrades as well.
As for the cost of one of these new aircraft , that, naturally, depends on a lot of factors. The starting price for the 737 MAX is of around $100 million, but the final cost can be, in some cases, some 30 percent higher than that.

Ferrari’s first electric car, the Luce, will start at $560,800 in the US, with American deliveries planned for the second quarter of 2027. Car and Driver first reported the figure, and Ferrari has confirmed it.
That’s roughly $80,000 under the ~$640,000 number that has followed the Luce since its unveiling in May, including in our own coverage. But Americans aren’t getting a deal.
Where the $640,000 came from
Ferrari didn’t give a US price when it launched the Luce in Rome on May 25 . It gave a European one: €550,000. Most outlets, us included, ran that through the exchange rate of the day, about $1.16 per euro, and got to roughly $640,000.
The problem is that European car prices are normally quoted with VAT included, and Italy’s rate is 22%.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Take the tax out and the Luce costs about €450,800 in Italy. At today’s rate of roughly $1.12 per euro, that’s around $506,000. So the US price is about $55,000 higher than what an Italian buyer pays before taxes, and American buyers still owe state sales tax on top of the $560,800.
Some of that gap is trade policy. European-built cars now face a 15% US tariff, and Ferrari already raised prices on part of its US lineup last year to cover it. The $560,800 also doesn’t include options, and Ferrari hasn’t published what those cost. Nobody buys a base Ferrari.
Sold out before the first US delivery
None of this will slow sales. Ferrari sold out its 2026 Luce allocation of just under 500 units in less than two months, with China doing a lot of the heavy lifting. In August, the first production chassis went for $40 million at a charity auction for the Ferrari Foundation.
That’s despite a rough reveal. The design, done with Jony Ive and Marc Newson’s LoveFrom, got hammered online, and Ferrari’s stock dropped sharply in the days after the launch before recovering.
The hardware is serious. The Luce uses four motors, one per wheel, for 1,035 hp combined. It’s built on an 800V architecture with a 122 kWh battery pack from SK On, charges at up to 350 kW, and Ferrari rates it at 529 km (329 miles) WLTP. It does 0-100 km/h in 2.5 seconds and weighs 2,260 kg (4,982 lb). It’s also Ferrari’s first five-seater.
For comparison, a Lucid Air Sapphire with over 1,200 hp costs around $250,000. You could buy two and still have change left over.

We’re not convinced every one of those orders comes from love of the car. Ferrari’s allocation game rewards loyal customers, and some buyers are surely taking a Luce to stay in line for the next limited-run V12. But a deposit is a deposit.

A combination of the personalized cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and Merck’s Keytruda just barely cleared analysts’ expectations for recurrence-free survival, leaving questions as to its applicability to tumor types beyond melanoma.
Data for Merck and Moderna’s highly anticipated personalized cancer vaccine leaked online Thursday morning, days ahead of a headlining reveal at the European Society of Medical Oncology meeting in Spain. The results left analysts disappointed—and hoping that the real presentation might be more optimistic.
Analysts had been hoping to see a recurrence-free survival (RFS) hazard ratio below 0.60 for the combination of intismeran autogene and Merck’s immuno-oncology blockbuster Keytruda. According to the leaked results, which were quickly removed after the erroneous posting, the combo achieved a 0.58 hazard ratio, reducing the risk of recurrence or death by 42%.
“Investors were looking for these data to demonstrate a benefit in melanoma but also read to efficacy in other tumors,” BMO Capital Markets wrote on Thursday afternoon. “These results are not enough to drive confidence amidst elevated expectations.”
The leak also revealed that 82.2% of patients who received the vaccine combo were alive after two years of treatment, which is higher than the 70% achieved by Keytruda alone, BMO said. The risk of distant metastases or death dropped by 38%.
“Taken together, we see support for intismeran autogene providing a benefit across both measures of distant metastases and measures of survival, supporting a potential commercial opportunity for the combination regimen,” BMO said.
Merck went ahead and posted a press release with the data on Thursday afternoon. Prior to the presentation, the company told BioSpace in an interview that the results had met their bar for efficacy, with Jane Healy, Merck’s head of oncology early clinical development, heralding the moment as the culmination of decades of learning in oncology.
“This is not a subtle benefit,” she said. “It’s really exciting to have all these advancements in genome sciences and AI and machine learning, which is very much part of the algorithm in IO therapy, and mRNA technology, that have all come together to give [patients] something that is very specific for their cancer.”
However, investors appeared to have been pinning their hopes on an earlier Phase 2 study, in which the combo achieved a hazard ratio of 0.51, according to RBC Capital Markets in a Thursday afternoon note. Investors had therefore hoped for the Phase 3 result to land between 0.50-0.59, putting the 0.58 “at the low end of expectations.
“While approval seems likely, commercial success is far less certain. The data raises fundamental questions about INT’s value proposition relative to standards of care, particularly neoadjuvant immunotherapy, which produces similar efficacy at potentially much less cost,” RBC wrote.
Shares of both Merck and Moderna declined after the leak. Merck fell by just over 1% to $147.93—with a sharp pitch into the red around the time the data leaked. Moderna, which has been looking to the vaccine for its post-COVID comeback, dropped more significantly in the aftermath of the release by 21% to $193.65 apiece.
Big reputation
The full dataset for the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial was set to be published on Saturday at the ESMO Congress. The companies announced the headline news that the trial met its primary endpoint in August, but investors were looking to this readout for more specific details. At the time, both Moderna and Merck enjoyed a market surge on the news as investors had been cautious about the personalized vaccine’s potential.

With expectations now sky high, the full data landed with a thud.
“While Merck shares appear to be reacting negatively to this hazard ratio, we assert this relative reduction in recurrence/death is clinically meaningful,” BMO wrote. “Such a reaction likely reflects inflated expectations into the full data release, rather than a true indictment on the efficacy of the combo therapy.”
With that said, BMO noted that Keytruda alone offered prior to surgery reached the same hazard ratio as compared to offering the therapy after surgery during prior Phase 2 trials. This could raise “questions on the need for added intismeran therapy,” the firm said.
Overall survival data were not yet available, Healy said. Analysts searched the data for scraps of information on this endpoint anyway, with RBC suggesting that the trend appears to be favorable.
William Blair was a bit more pragmatic on the data leak, pointing to the fact that Moderna’s shares are still up 525% this year even with the reduction today.
“The information also suggests efficacy was similar across lower and higher disease groups; we wonder if that is an indication of efficacy across patients with differing tumor mutational burden,” the firm offered.

The Phase 3 data expanded the program into more than a thousand patients, adding more different stages of disease to provide a larger potential patient population, Healy explained.
“[The study] showed that regardless of whether they were high risk, metastatic stage—which is the highest risk—or if they were [stage] 2b versus 3, they all had the same opportunity to benefit from the therapy, according to the results,” Healy said, adding that there weren’t any other major subgroup differences either.

AbbVie is eyeing regulatory filings in 2027 for the skin disease drug lutikizumab after clearing multiple endpoints in a late-stage trial, but the results have disappointed some analysts, raising questions about its commercial prospects.
AbbVie’s investigational IL-1α/β inhibitor designed to treat a painful inflammatory skin condition reduced abscesses and other symptoms, meeting the main goal of a Phase 3 trial, though the result fell below analyst expectations set by earlier data.
AbbVie’s Phase 3 INTREPID study evaluated lutikizumab, a dual-variable-domain immunoglobulin taking aim at IL-1α and IL-1β—two key inflammatory cytokines . The trial recruited about 1,400 patients with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), a chronic disease that causes painful cysts and abscesses and can lead to irreversible skin damage.
Patients receiving lutikizumab demonstrated a 31.4% response rate in abscess and nodule count reduction at week 16. The reduction compares to a 23.4% decrease seen for patients on placebo, a statistically significant difference of 8%.
Analysts with Guggenheim Partners called the placebo-adjusted response rate “disappointing,” citing significant degradation from mid-phase data , when lutikizumab elicited a 28% improvement over placebo.
Analysts at BMO Capital Markets were more bullish, writing in a Thursday note to investors that AbbVie’s late-stage findings validate “efficacy of IL-1α/β inhibition in HS, potentially expanding treatment with a new mechanism.” The current leading HS treatment is UCB’s Bimzelx, an IL-17 targeting antibody that led to a 20% placebo-adjusted response rate at week 16 . Meanwhile, Merck recently shared competitive mid-stage data for its anti-TL1A tulisokibart, achieving about a 25% placebo-adjusted reduction in HS.
Drug Development
Merck’s antibody impresses with ‘highly competitive’ data in chronic skin disease
Merck has revealed detailed data for tulisokibart from a mid-stage trial in hidradenitis suppurativa that analysts say could help carve out a place in a crowded market that already includes AbbVie’s Humira and UCB’s Bimzelx.
October 1, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
Despite the lower response rate than competitors, the achievement of eight secondary endpoints for lutikizumab strengthen its overall profile, with BMO analysts citing reductions in both pain and flares. The drug’s clean safety profile also supports potential broad use as a chronic therapy, BMO added.
Overall, the Phase 3 efficacy demonstrated by lutikizumab “could expand the treatment landscape in HS for patients in need of an alternative mechanism,” BMO said.
Both analysts were intrigued by AbbVie’s newly announced plans to combine lutikizumab with its long-acting amylin analog ABBV-295 later this year, plus the potential to pair with the anti-TL1A antibody ABBV-701 “to address multiple disease pathways that may improve outcomes for patients living with HS,” according to the pharma’s Thursday release.
AbbVie is expected to share 36-week blinded extension data for lutikizumab next year—findings the pharma said could be used to support regulatory filings in the second half of 2027. Analysts are looking to the additional data to provide clarity on the drug’s durability, long-term safety and commercial positioning.
“While the results could be sufficient to support regulatory approval, we think that given the topline Phase 3 data reported today, commercial uptake for luti monotherapy in HS will likely be limited,” Guggenheim wrote.
Making waves for other HS developers
The mixed data sent waves across the market for other drugmakers in the space.
“While the study was technically positive, results were disappointing relative to Phase 2 and investor expectations,” Leerink Partners analysts wrote, citing the AbbVie readout as “a key external catalyst” for Avalo Therapeutics, which is developing abdakibart, an IL-1β antagonist, for HS.
Given the partial overlap between the two candidates’ mechanisms of action, Avalo’s shares sunk more than 36% on Thursday, a reaction Leerink called “overdone.” The analysts instead view the “underwhelming lutikizumab results as an opportunity for greater differentiation and competitive positioning for abdakibart.”
Avalo’s most advanced asset, abdakibart is expected to enter Phase 3 testing in the first half of 2027. Avalo’s drug has the potential to be dosed less frequently than lutikizumab. In a Phase 2 trial , abdakibart reduced HS abscesses and nodules by about 42% as compared to 25.6% for placebo.

Norfolk Southern’s third-quarter profits rose as higher volume and rates, and fuel surcharges, produced record revenue.
“Our third quarter was strong with steady execution, making notable improvements to our network while delivering solid results,” Chief Executive Mark George said on the railroad’s earnings call. “We have an outstanding team of thoroughbreds who remain focused on the fundamentals: operating a safe, reliable railroad, serving our customers, growing the business, and improving productivity across the network.”
Operating income increased 5% to $1.15 billion, as revenue grew 14% to $3.52 billion. Fuel surcharge revenue was responsible for 8 of the 14 points of revenue growth. Earnings per share rose 7%, to $3.37.
The railroad’s (NYSE: NSC ) operating ratio was 67.4%, up 2.8 points from a year ago largely due to higher fuel costs. Adjusted for the impact of ongoing costs related to the February 2023 derailment and hazardous materials release in East Palestine, Ohio, and expenses related to the proposed merger with Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP ), the operating ratio was 65.4%.
Overall volume was up 3% for the quarter, with merchandise, intermodal , and coal volume all up 3%.
“Demand for rail service is growing with encouraging trends in areas such as domestic intermodal and chemicals,” George said. “The current macro environment is tightening the truck market, and that helps rail be more competitive. And what you saw in the quarter is us capturing the increased customer demand.”
Chief Commercial Officer Ed Elkins said NS is broadly optimistic for the rest of 2026. High fuel prices tied to the Middle East conflict are boosting energy-related traffic. But NS is watching whether prolonged high gas prices eventually soften consumer demand.
A tight truck market and high fuel costs favor highway-to-rail conversions in forest products, consumer products, and domestic intermodal, Elkins said. International intermodal remains weighed down by trade uncertainty. Manufacturing has expanded nine straight months, industrial development is ahead of last year, and vehicle production looks modestly positive. Coal is expected to grow, led by exports and supported by utilities replenishing depleted stockpiles.
NS has rolled out new online customer tools that speed responses to rate requests and provide better shipment visibility.
“The result is more accurate and more actionable shipment information, enabling customers to plan more effectively, operate more efficiently, and ultimately make decisions with greater confidence,” Elkins said. “As these capabilities continue to scale, our goal is simple: Make Norfolk Southern the easiest railroad to do business with so that we win more freight in competitive markets.”
Key operational metrics were down compared to a year ago but improved over the second quarter, when spot crew shortages led to congestion. Terminal dwell improved 3% and train speed was up 5% compared to the second quarter. On-time train originations improved 18%.
“Our railroaders managed another demanding quarter, overcoming significant weather and operating disruptions while remaining focused on serving our customers and operating safely,” Chief Operating Officer Brian Barr said.
The intermodal service composite was 84%, down from 92% a year ago. Merchandise trip plan compliance was 74%, down from 80% a year ago. Compared to the second quarter, merchandise plan compliance rose 6 points, while the intermodal metric declined by a point.
“We entered the quarter with a clear plan to recover network fluidity by improving originations, reducing dwell, increasing velocity, and getting the railroad back on schedule,” Barr said. “We delivered sequential improvement across those foundational measures.”
The improvements in the quarter came despite weather-related disruptions in August.
“On our network’s high-speed corridor, the team quickly restored infrastructure, removing hundreds of downed trees, repairing multiple washouts, and handling widespread power outages by activating strategic reroutes and repositioning resources,” Barr said. “While the historic wind and rain interrupted some of our July momentum, it did not derail our progress.”
One way NS reduced dwell was by redesigning car connections at terminals, which eliminated handlings. The changes removed 95 crew starts per week and took 200 cars per day off the network, while the railroad absorbed 3% carload growth, Barr said.
NS also consolidated smaller trains between Birmingham, Ala., and Macon, Ga., saving 14 crew starts per week while reducing locomotive needs. Shifting 50 daily switch cars from Enola, Pa., to Allentown Yard freed up Enola crews for road service and moved the switching to a yard with a lower cost per car. It also opens up yard capacity in Enola, Barr said.
The railroad’s personal injury and train accident rates continued to show improvement through the first nine months of the year. The train accident rate was at a record low for the railroad.
